Abstract

This paper focuses on a conformal block with rank 3 2 3 2 \frac{3}{2} divide start_ARG 3 end_ARG start_ARG 2 end_ARG irregular singularity
which corresponds to the prepotential of the ℋ 1 subscript ℋ 1 {\cal H}_{1} caligraphic_H start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 1 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT Argyres-Douglas theory in Ω Ω \Omega roman_Ω background.
We derive this irregular conformal block using generalized holomorphic anomaly recursion relation. This results is an expression
which is a power series in Ω Ω \Omega roman_Ω -background parameters ϵ 1 , 2 subscript italic-ϵ 1 2 \epsilon_{1,2} italic_ϵ start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 1 , 2 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT and exact in coupling.
We have verified that in small coupling regime our result is consistent with previously known expressions.

Furthermore we derive the Deformed Seiberg-Witten curve which provides an alternative tool to explore above
mentioned theory in Nekrasov-Shatashvili limit of Ω Ω \Omega roman_Ω -background.
We checked that the results are in complete agreement with the holomorphic anomaly approach.

1 Introduction

Equivariant localization is a powerful technique to investigate supersymmetric theories. In particular
its application to Seiberg-Witten (SW) theory Seiberg:1994rs ; Seiberg:1994aj allows one to reduce seemingly intractable instanton
moduli integrals to essentially smaller submanifold of instantons invariant with respect to an Abelian
subgroup of global gauge singled out by the adjoint scalar VEV Bellisai:2000bc ; Flume:2001kb ; Flume:2001nc ; Dorey:2002ik . Embedding the theory in a specific
graviphoton (so called Ω Ω \Omega roman_Ω -) background leads to further drastic simplifications. From the localization
point of view this amounts to incorporating (Euclidean) space-time rotations on two orthogonal planes parameterized
by the angles ϵ 1 subscript italic-ϵ 1 \epsilon_{1} italic_ϵ start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 1 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT , ϵ 2 subscript italic-ϵ 2 \epsilon_{2} italic_ϵ start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 2 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT with global gauge transformations. As a result, the integrals mentioned above localize in
each instanton sector to a finite number of fixed points, which are labeled by Young diagrams.
One recovers the initial SW theory by
simply sending the Ω Ω \Omega roman_Ω -background parameters ϵ 1 , 2 subscript italic-ϵ 1 2 \epsilon_{1,2} italic_ϵ start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 1 , 2 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT to zero.
For explicit computations, various localization techniques have been developed
Nekrasov:2002qd ; Flume:2002az ; Bruzzo:2002xf ; Nekrasov:2003rj ; Flume:2004rp .

Over time, it has been realized that the partition function of the gauge theory in
Ω Ω \Omega roman_Ω -background can be mapped into correlation functions of two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT)
Gaiotto:2009we ; Alday:2009aq ; Poghossian:2009mk . This remarkable correspondence is referred as AGT
(Alday, Gaiotto, Tachikawa) duality.

On the other hand it was demonstrated by Argyres and Douglas Argyres:1995jj three decades ago, that
there are specific points in the moduli space of certain 𝒩 = 2 𝒩 2 {\cal N}=2 caligraphic_N = 2 supersymmetric gauge theories,
commonly referred as Argyres-Douglas points, where both electrically and magnetically charged particles
become massless simultaneously.

It appears that the partition functions of Argyres-Douglas theories in presence of
Ω Ω \Omega roman_Ω -background, from 2d CFT point of view corresponds
to conformal blocks of so called irregular states.
These new class of states (called rank r 𝑟 r italic_r irregular states) were
introduced in Gaiotto:2009ma ; Gaiotto:2012sf ,
where a systematic method was developed
for constructing integer rank r 𝑟 r italic_r irregular states in 2d Liouville CFT
by colliding insertion points of r + 1 𝑟 1 r+1 italic_r + 1 primary fields. Detailed investigations of relations between
irregular blocks and AD theories were further carried out in
Nishinaka:2012kn ; Kanno:2013vi ; Bonelli:2016qwg ; Nishinaka:2019nuy ; Kimura:2020krd ; Bonelli:2021uvf ; Bonelli:2022ten ; Kimura:2022yua ; Consoli:2022eey ; Fucito:2023plp .

In Poghosyan:2023zvy the simplest AD theory ℋ 0 subscript ℋ 0 {\cal H}_{0} caligraphic_H start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 0 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT related
to rank 5 2 5 2 \frac{5}{2} divide start_ARG 5 end_ARG start_ARG 2 end_ARG conformal block, was included coherently into
above scheme and in-depth analysis was carried out for the corresponding irregular conformal block.
This allowed Hamachika:2024efr to give
a definition for arbitrary half integer rank irregular states.

The focus of this paper is the rank 3 2 3 2 \frac{3}{2} divide start_ARG 3 end_ARG start_ARG 2 end_ARG irregular conformal block

Notice that we have chosen both primary and irregular state parameters to take the same value β 0 subscript 𝛽 0 \beta_{0} italic_β start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 0 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT ,
otherwise from standard CFT arguments the irregular block would vanish.
Using the holomorphic anomaly recursion relation Huang:2006si ; Huang:2009md ; Huang:2011qx ; Huang:2013eja
we have found this irregular conformal block up to order 8 8 8 8 in ϵ 1 , 2 subscript italic-ϵ 1 2 \epsilon_{1,2} italic_ϵ start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 1 , 2 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT . It is important to
emphasize that the less standard form of its discriminant made the application of the recursion relation
more complicated.
Our result ( 59 ) after expanding it in Λ 3 subscript Λ 3 \Lambda_{3} roman_Λ start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 3 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT perfectly match with those obtained through
irregular state computation carried out in Hamachika:2024efr or ( 2 ).

In Poghossian:2010pn ; Fucito:2011pn ; Nekrasov:2013xda , the concept of a so-called Deformed Seiberg-Witten (DSW) curve was introduced
(see also Poghosyan:2020zzg ). This method provides an efficient method to investigate gauge theories in
particular case of Ω Ω \Omega roman_Ω -background when one of the deformation parameters, say ϵ 1 = 0 subscript italic-ϵ 1 0 \epsilon_{1}=0 italic_ϵ start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 1 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT = 0 (Nekrasov-Shatashvili
limit Nekrasov:2009rc ). We have derived DSW curve equation for our present case of interest the ℋ 1 subscript ℋ 1 {\cal H}_{1} caligraphic_H start_POSTSUBSCRIPT 1 end_POSTSUBSCRIPT theory and then used it to
derive the deformed prepotential and corresponding heavy conformal block.

This paper is structured as follows:
In Section 2 , we provide a review of the r = 3 2 𝑟 3 2 r=\frac{3}{2} italic_r = divide start_ARG 3 end_ARG start_ARG 2 end_ARG irregular state and its corresponding conformal block.
Section 3 begins with an overview of the holomorphic anomaly recursion relation.
In Subsection 3.3 , we outline the framework for applying this recursion to our specific case.
Our results are presented in Subsection 3.4 .
In Section 4 , we derive the analog of the Belavin–Polyakov–Zamolodchikov (BPZ) differential equation for rank 3 / 2 3 2 3/2 3 / 2 ,
and subsequently explore its heavy limit. From this differential equation, we determine the DSW curve, which enables us to derive the heavy conformal block.
The appendices provide detailed computations and results that were too extensive to be included in the main text.
